full_judgment:
12. The fundamental and basic presumption in the administration of criminal law and justice delivery system is that the accused should be presumed to be innocent till the charges are proved beyond reasonable doubt on the basis of clear, cogent, credible or unimpeachable evidence. In a criminal trial, the burden of proving guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt always rests on the prose-cu lion and on its failure; it cannot fall back upon the evidence adduced by the accused in support of his defence to rest its case solely thereon. The party on whom the onus of proof lies must in order to succeed must have to prove the prosecution case beyond reason-able doubt. He cannot on his failure to do so advantage of the weakness of the defence case. He must be succeeded by the strength of his own evidence and the clearness of its own prove. 

 25. It appears from the evidence on record that in the instant case formalities under section 164 and 364 have not been observed the alleged confessional statement is inadmissible and no presumption can be raised under section 80 of the Evidence Act.
